attackVerdicts.attack: DB-1: exec_command env-overlay fix via DEFAULT_ENV_ALLOWLIST over-restricts and guts the tool's documented 64-arbitrary-env feature
attackVerdicts.evidence: Probe p4 (real code): handleExecCommand({command:'printf %s "$CFLAGS">out',env:{CFLAGS:'-O2'}}) writes '-O2' to the child today — arbitrary declared env reaches the child. buildPtyEnv({parentEnv,declared:{CFLAGS,MYVAR,PYTHONPATH,BASH_ENV,HOME,PATH},inheritEnv:false}) returns keys {PATH,HOME,PYTHONPATH} only — CFLAGS/MYVAR/BASH_ENV all DROPPED. Schema tools-6.ts:83-88 documents 'a child shell that needs more than 64 NEW env vars'. Routing the overlay through the ~18-name DEFAULT_ENV_ALLOWLIST (env-scrub.ts:44-68) silently drops legit CFLAGS/MYVAR and — critically for bench — every per-repo build var. The code-injection channel is real (probe: BASH_ENV=rc.sh and HOME=fakehome/.bash_profile markers BOTH created via bash -lc login shell). Correct fix is a code-injecting-NAME denylist (BASH_ENV/ENV/SHELLOPTS/PS4/BASH_FUNC_*/LD_PRELOAD/DYLD_*/IFS + HOME must be handled), preserving the arbitrary overlay.

attackVerdicts.attack: DB-2: SEC-4 bypass-immune ASK floor flips legitimate scripted cleanup ADMIT→DENY inside the bench/eval lane
attackVerdicts.evidence: config-build.ts:721 mode='acceptEdits' + :619 onConfirm:async()=>false. Probe p3 (real runAdmissibilityGate over [bash,...6-tool]): rm -rf "$BUILD_DIR", rm -rf "$@", cd "$T"&&rm -rf *, rm -rf "$DIR"/* ALL ADMIT today under acceptEdits+onConfirm=false; assessShellCommand on each = 'unknown'. Under R1's floor these become the new kind→ask→onConfirm(false)→DENY. R1's compat/risks sections frame fail-closed deny for 'headless/SDK/non-TTY' and never name the bench lane's auto-declining onConfirm — a no-real-operator surface that decision (a) says must deny. This is a default-ON, bench-affecting change with UNMEASURED pass-rate impact (MEASURE-FIRST). NOTE: Claude Code (CJ→xU ask, QJ non-interactive→deny) has the SAME tension, so the direction is defensible parity — but it must be measured or gated, not shipped default-ON blind.

revisedDesign.summary: Split into SEC-3 (unconditional, bench-neutral, ship now) and SEC-4 (bench-affecting, gated on measurement + decisions). SEC-3: declare write_stdin.extractShellCommand on the SAME registry port HARD_DENY/actionKeyOf/the ownership fence already read; move the completeness census to the assembled universe (dedup, full KNOWN set); fix exec_command's env overlay via a code-injecting-name DENYLIST (NOT DEFAULT_ENV_ALLOWLIST, which guts the 64-arbitrary-env feature and bench). SEC-4: add ONE new ShellAssessmentKind 'ask-destructive-unresolved' emitted ONLY by destructive assessors with an unresolvable target (recursive+force delete, xargs→rm/sh, chmod/chown -R unresolvable, cd-into-unknown+glob — NOT assessFind, which the regex hard-denies first), consumed by ONE new gate floor-step over the already-resolved action.shellCommand — appealable by a real operator, bypass-immune AND autoApprove-immune, fail-closed to deny with no operator. This corrects R1's over-invasive evaluate/evaluateStack/evaluateAuto triple edit and its mischaracterization of the confirm:'sensitive' reuse.
revisedDesign.structuralMechanism: (1) SSOT extractor: write_stdin joins bash/pty_write/exec_command/test_runner/container_*/shadow_verify as an extractShellCommand-declaring tool, so ToolAction.shellCommand — the single value HARD_DENY, actionKeyOf and the fence read — is populated; the bare 'write_stdin' grant becomes content-keyed. (2) New verdict as a closed-union member: ShellAssessmentKind gains 'ask-destructive-unresolved', added to the exhaustive RANK Record<ShellAssessmentKind,number> (ranked 2.5, between unknown=2 and hard-deny=3) with a runtime drift-guard so tsc+runtime force every consumer to handle it; only the destructive assessors emit it, benign-unreadable (git/diskutil unknown) and safe-unreadable (cat/tar) are untouched. (3) ONE floor consumer at the single production chokepoint: a new gate step runShellFloorGate (sibling of runHandoffFloorGate) consults a new pure @/permission export shellFloorReason(action)=non-null iff assessShellCommand(action.shellCommand).kind==='ask-destructive-unresolved'; it routes through the existing resolveAskBranch (onConfirm→approve, no-onConfirm→deny fail-closed) and does NOT fall through under bypass or autoApprove — mirroring Claude Code's bypassImmune dangerousRemoval circuit breaker + QJ non-interactive→deny, without hand-off-required's unappealability. evaluate/evaluateStack/evaluateAuto and hardDenyReason stay byte-identical. (4) exec_command env: overlay through a code-injecting-name denylist, preserving arbitrary declared vars.

changes.change: SEC-3a: pass the 8th arg to make('write_stdin',…): extractShellCommand:(input)=>typeof (input as {data?:unknown}).data==='string' ? input.data : null — mirrors pty_write. Populates shellCommand for HARD_DENY, the fence, and content grants; auto-fixes the bare-'write_stdin' [a]lways amplifier.

SEC-3b: change census surface from buildDefaultTools to assembleToolUniverse; de-duplicate names before comparison; set KNOWN = {bash,test_runner,pty_write,write_stdin,exec_command,container_exec,container_write_file,shadow_verify} each with danger/benign/expectedExtract probes; add run_tests+node_repl+send_input to NON_CHANNEL_ALLOWLIST with reasons (argv/JS/agent-message, not shell-string); keep strict set-equality after dedup + the smell backstop.

SEC-3c: replace {...scrubEnvFrom(process.env),...(input.env??{})} with an overlay that first scrubs the parent, then merges input.env MINUS a code-injecting-name denylist {BASH_ENV,ENV,SHELLOPTS,BASHOPTS,PS4,IFS,LD_PRELOAD,LD_LIBRARY_PATH,DYLD_*,BASH_FUNC_*,HOME? (drop HOME override — bash -lc sources .bash_profile)}. Preserves CFLAGS/MYVAR/PYTHONPATH etc. SEC-3d (separate commit): route the Bun.spawn(['bash','-lc',cmd]) through getShellSandbox()/wrapSandboxArgv like runShell, or document+test the residual — verify no regression on the PTY-retain/grace path first.

SEC-4: add 'ask-destructive-unresolved' to ShellAssessmentKind + an askUnresolved(rule,reason) constructor + a RANK entry (2.5-slot). Emit it INSTEAD OF unknown() in: assessDelete (recursive&&forced && unresolved/unknown-cwd operand only — leaves rm -f "$LOG" as unknown), stdinOperandVerdict (xargs→rm/sh), assessSimple (chmod/chown -R with unresolved operand), and the cd-into-unknown+glob delete path. Do NOT touch assessFind (find-action-flag-set regex hard-denies first — dead code). Leave every non-destructive unknown (git/diskutil) and safe (cat/tar) unchanged.

SEC-4: export shellFloorReason(action):{rule,reason}|null = non-null iff assessShellCommand(action.shellCommand).kind==='ask-destructive-unresolved'. hardDenyReason stays hard-deny-only (monotonic). Add the RANK runtime drift-guard beside RANK (Object.keys(RANK) must equal the ShellAssessmentKind members).

SEC-4: add runShellFloorGate(call,config,permission,action,opts): if shellFloorReason(action)!==null, route through resolveAskBranch (onConfirm→approve admits; absent/decline→deny fail-closed). Do NOT fall through under bypass/acceptEdits, and do NOT honor hitl.autoApprove for this floor (distinct from the confirm:'sensitive' universal floor at line 202). Export it.

SEC-4: wire runShellFloorGate immediately AFTER runHandoffFloorGate (step ~2.15), before runPermissionRequestHook/toolProfile/pattern/rules/HITL/stack/mode — so every mode converges on it after HARD_DENY and it precedes every allow-capable path.

SEC-3 hardening: suppress the [P] prefix-grant verb for stdin channels (write_stdin/pty_write) — a keystroke fragment's program token is meaningless (probe: 'write_stdin|y'→'y'); offer content-keyed [a]lways only. SSOT the stdin-tool set next to KNOWN_SHELL_INPUT stdin subset.

Add a per-session (per-pid/per-handle) logical-line buffer that assembles fragmented writes up to a newline, rejects NUL and raw editing control bytes (Codex #41354 parity), and feeds the assembled line to shellFloorReason/HARD_DENY. write_stdin needs the buffer pty_write already has; unify both on one 'assess bytes into a child stdin' helper (Codex 'one assessment path'). Full tty line-editor emulation stays out of scope (documented residual).

reusedExisting: ToolAction.shellCommand + ToolRegistry.extractShellCommand (the SSOT port; withResolvedShellCommand already resolves it uniformly at gate entry)
actionKeyOf content-keying (auto-fixes the [a]lways amplifier once the extractor exists)
assessShellCommand + the exhaustive RANK Record + runtime drift-guard culture (exhaustive-record-classification-drift-guard)
resolveAskBranch's onConfirm→approve / no-operator→deny pipeline (no bespoke deny logic)
the runHandoffFloorGate 'floor pulled ahead of allow-capable gates' pattern (the new floor step is its sibling)
the assembled-tool-universe fixture as the census surface
pty_write's projectPtyInput/pendingInput per-handle buffer as the model for write_stdin's logical-line assembly
scrubEnvFrom leaf (parent scrub stays); only the input.env overlay gets a denylist
revisedDesign.compatibilityAndMigration: SEC-3 is byte-identical for every non-attack path: HARD_DENY unchanged (monotonic), the census only widens KNOWN to tools already declaring the method, and the env denylist preserves CFLAGS/MYVAR/PYTHONPATH (only code-injecting names dropped — no legit SWE-bench build var affected). The one SEC-3 behavior change: literal HARD_DENY commands (rm -rf ~, curl|sh) typed into a PTY via write_stdin are now blocked in every mode. SEC-4 adds ONLY asks for recursive+force/xargs-rm/chmod-R/cd+glob with an unresolvable target; benign-unreadable (cat "$X", git "$SUB" status) and resolvable/relative (rm -rf ./build) are byte-identical paired controls. The SEC-4 behavior change (a destructive-unresolved command now prompts under bypass/acceptEdits and denies with no operator) is the intended N16 parity and MUST be measured on the bench smoke baseline before default-ON.
revisedDesign.userVisibleBehavior: SEC-3: a model typing rm -rf ~ (or any HARD_DENY command) into an attached PTY via write_stdin is blocked in every mode (was silently allowed under bypass); a single [a]lways on write_stdin no longer blanket-covers all later bytes; exec_command env can no longer smuggle BASH_ENV/LD_PRELOAD code. SEC-4: a generated rm -rf "$@" / rm -rf "$BUILD_DIR" / cd "$T"&&rm -rf * prompts even under bypass and is denied (appealable, operator can approve) in headless/SDK/bench, instead of running silently; ordinary rm -rf ./build, cat "$X", git status unchanged.
revisedDesign.rollout: SEC-3 (extractor + census + env denylist + prefix-verb suppression) DEFAULT-ON unconditionally — a security floor, bench-neutral by construction (no legit trajectory types a HARD_DENY command into stdin or declares BASH_ENV). exec_command OS-sandbox routing (SEC-3d) is a separate commit, verified for regression or documented as a tested residual. SEC-4 floor: land the assessment + gate wiring behind a MEASURE-FIRST gate — run the SWE-bench smoke baseline (tests/smoke/swebench) with the floor on vs off and confirm no pass-rate regression from denied cleanup before flipping default-ON; the only tunable is the static, reviewed SET of destructive heads (no runtime knob that could silently disable the floor).
revisedDesign.costEstimate: SEC-3a extractor = XS. SEC-3b census move = S (classify each newly-visible declaring tool + dedup). SEC-3c env denylist = S. SEC-3d sandbox routing = M (must not regress PTY-retain). SEC-4 new kind + drift guard + assessor edits + one gate step = M (closed-union → several red-on-injection tests). Option D logical-line assembly + NUL/control rejection = M.

userDecisions.question: SEC-4 floor default-ON now, or land behind a MEASURE-FIRST gate on the SWE-bench smoke baseline?
userDecisions.options: (a) default-ON immediately; (b) implement + tests green, but measure smoke pass-rate (floor on vs off) and only flip default-ON after confirming no regression from denied cleanup
userDecisions.recommendation: (b). config-build.ts wires acceptEdits + onConfirm:async()=>false; probe p3 proves rm -rf "$BUILD_DIR"/"$@"/cd+glob currently ADMIT there and would flip to DENY. Memory rule: measure before a bench-affecting default-ON change; SEC-3 ships now (bench-neutral), SEC-4 waits on the measurement.

userDecisions.question: When a floored destructive-unresolved command reaches an AUTONOMOUS surface with no real operator (headless / SDK-embed autoApprove:true / bench onConfirm:false / non-TTY bypass), deny or allow?
userDecisions.options: (a) DENY (fail-closed; Claude Code QJ parity — non-interactive dangerous removal → deny); (b) allow (preserve today's silent-run)
userDecisions.recommendation: (a) DENY, and make the floor autoApprove-immune (distinct from confirm:'sensitive' which gates.ts:202 opts out under autoApprove). A destructive command whose blast radius we cannot read, with nobody to ask, must not run unattended. This is the exact path SEC-4 targets (embed.ts:161 sets autoApprove:true). Couple with decision 1's measurement so the bench cost is known.

userDecisions.question: SEC-4 floor breadth — which destructive shapes fire when the target is unresolvable?
userDecisions.options: (a) recursive+force delete only (rm -rf/rimraf/shred); (b) + xargs→rm/sh, chmod/chown -R, cd-into-unknown+glob; (c) also single-file (rm -f "$LOG", unlink, rmdir)
userDecisions.recommendation: (b). Matches Claude Code N16 (recursive/mass-deletion + positional/possibly-empty var). Excludes single-file (c) so ordinary rm -f "$LOG" scripted cleanup is not prompted (probe p1 confirms rm -f "$LOG" stays plain unknown automatically since assessDelete only escalates on recursive&&forced). assessFind is EXCLUDED — the regex hard-denies it first (dead code, per MH-2).

userDecisions.question: exec_command OS-sandbox (SEC-3d): route through getShellSandbox now, or document + test as a residual?
userDecisions.options: (a) route now (parity with bash's runShell); (b) document + test the residual and defer
userDecisions.recommendation: (a) for the bash -lc spawn (it is a shell, same threat as bash) — but as its OWN commit, verified against the PTY-retain/grace path (not probed here; code-read only). The env-denylist fix (SEC-3c) ships regardless.

userDecisions.question: Option D (logical-line assembly + NUL/control rejection): block SEC-3 core, or fast-follow?
userDecisions.options: (a) fold into SEC-3 as one shared stdin path now; (b) fast-follow after SEC-3 extractor
userDecisions.recommendation: The task explicitly asks 'how every PTY-writing tool shares ONE assessment path assembling a logical command line'. Deliver at least the shared per-session line buffer + NUL rejection as commit 8 (not indefinitely deferred). Full tty line-editor emulation (^U/DEL/bracketed-paste) stays a documented residual — the OS sandbox is the real boundary there.

residualRisks: Interpreter REPL payloads (python3 -i/node/perl) via write_stdin/pty_write into a retained child are not shell; the shell grammar reads shutil.rmtree(...) as safe-known and the content-only extractor cannot know the PTY's foreground process. The PtyTable slot DOES store the launch command (exec-command.ts:24) — an unused signal; the principled follow-up is to mark interpreter-launched retained sessions always-confirm (as node_repl already is). Not closed by SEC-3/SEC-4.

Raw-byte stdin assessment is best-effort vs tty line editing (^U/DEL/bracketed-paste); Option D closes the accidental split-write/NUL cases but a determined adversary on a live interactive shell can construct a logical line whose raw form assesses differently (R1 p4). The OS sandbox is the real boundary — and exec_command doesn't use it until SEC-3d.

SEC-4 floor at gate step ~2.15 precedes the (default-OFF) post-denial-override axis in evaluateStack, so a user who override-approved a specific action-signature is re-asked for a destructive-unresolved command. PLAUSIBLE-UNMEASURED (not driven end-to-end); arguably correct (a stale override should not authorize a different unresolved blast radius).

Regex HARD_DENY over-matches multi-line/chained benign commands (probe p6: 'rm -rf ./build\nls ~\n' → hardDeny=true). Pre-existing, orthogonal to this cluster; noted so a test author does not mistake it for a new false positive.
exec_command SEC-3d sandbox routing correctness (no regression on PTY-retain/grace) is UNVERIFIED — code-read only that it bypasses the slot. Must be probed before landing commit 7.

The SEC-4 measurement (decision 1) has no local bench trajectory in-repo to replay; requires an actual SWE-bench smoke run (tests/smoke/swebench, gpt-5 baseline) — cannot be settled from static probes.
